editorNote: Examples and evidence are refreshed separately from the authored core analysis.

examples.summary: Finland tested a basic-income-style payment for unemployed participants, with the most widely cited findings showing improved wellbeing and limited headline employment effects relative to expectations of a dramatic labour-market shift.
lessons: Basic income can improve recipients' reported wellbeing and confidence even when employment effects are modest.
Short-term experiments are useful for delivery learning but do not fully answer how a permanent national UBI would interact with taxation and wider services.
sources: Kela - Results of Finland's basic income experiment
OECD - Basic Income as a Policy Option

examples.summary: GiveDirectly's long-duration study in Kenya is one of the most prominent efforts to test long-term unconditional transfers at scale, with research focused on consumption, resilience, investment, and community-level effects over time.
lessons: Longer-running transfers may tell policymakers more about adaptation, investment, and local spillovers than short pilot schemes.
Poverty-context cash studies are informative, but results should not be mapped mechanically onto high-income welfare states.

examples.status: Permanent annual dividend rather than full UBI
examples.summary: Alaska's Permanent Fund Dividend is often cited in UBI debates because it shows how a universal cash payment linked to a shared asset can become politically durable, even though it is not large enough to function as a full income floor.
lessons: Universal payments can attract durable public support when funded from a visible common-asset story.
A partial dividend model is politically and fiscally different from a full UBI intended to replace insecurity across the income distribution.

examples.summary: The Stockton Economic Empowerment Demonstration tested guaranteed income in a city setting and became influential in later US debates around no-strings-attached cash, financial volatility, and labour-market behaviour.
lessons: Small city pilots can shape political narratives even when they are not full universal programmes.
Guaranteed income evidence is often strongest on income volatility and wellbeing rather than on proving a single universal national template.

analysis.title: Simplicity and responsiveness pull in opposite directions
analysis.summary: International evidence keeps pointing to the same tension: flat universal payments are simple to administer and easy to understand, but households with high rent, disability-related costs, or care needs often still require layered support beyond any flat grant.
sources: OECD - Basic Income as a Policy Option
IMF - Universal Basic Income and Work

analysis.title: Pilots are politically valuable but analytically limited
analysis.summary: Experiments are useful for testing delivery, recipient experience, and some behavioural effects, but they do not fully reproduce the fiscal and macroeconomic environment of a permanent national reform funded through taxation.
sources: Kela - Results of Finland's basic income experiment

analysis.title: Funding story matters as much as payment design
analysis.summary: Comparative debates show that public support depends heavily on how a UBI is financed and what it replaces. The same headline payment can be understood as inclusive social insurance or as a route to cutting more responsive welfare institutions.
sources: IMF - Universal Basic Income and Work
Institute for Fiscal Studies - Welfare reform analysis
